text: Five episodes, each building on the last. We start with a problem, not with a file.
Two teams working apart both pick the most obvious field name there is. Nothing in either document warns you they meant different things.
Now the mirror image. One name meant two things. Here one thing is written three ways, in three different domains.
The obvious answer is to add a schema. So we add one, and watch how it handles the two documents from earlier.
That is not a failure of the schema. It is precisely what a schema was designed to do, and no more.
Now the other side. If shape is not meaning, then meaning has to come from somewhere else.
The same limit applies in reverse. Watch what this context will accept.
Set the two of them side by side, and the difference between them has a remarkably simple shape.
This is what it costs, long after the data was written.
Everything so far was the argument for this one sentence.
